findings.evidenceJa: 耳飾りからこぼれた液体が原因
findings.governingReading: The liquid spilled from Sakura’s earring caused her collapse; its precise nature is not stated here.
findings.explanation: A conditional English variant identifies the liquid categorically as poison.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔力……魔術回路が少なくなっていた
findings.governingReading: Rin begins to say magical power, then corrects herself to the more exact “Magic Circuits.”
findings.explanation: The English deletes Rin’s audible technical self-correction.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路を育ててきた
findings.governingReading: The bloodline cultivated magical circuits over generations.
findings.explanation: The English singularizes the inherited circuit system.

findings.highlight: I couldn’t go see her much
findings.evidenceJa: あの子とはまともに会えなかった
findings.governingReading: Rin could not meet or interact properly with Sakura after the adoption.
findings.explanation: The English reduces severed reciprocal contact to Rin not visiting often.

findings.highlight: A dim light shines into the gloom of my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 淀んでいた胸にかすかな光が射す
findings.governingReading: A faint light enters Shirou’s stagnant, darkened chest or heart.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the image from emotion to cognition and changes faint light to dim light.

findings.highlight: dispose of her, just like I would with any other enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 敵として処理する
findings.governingReading: Rin says she will deal with Sakura as an enemy if Sakura cannot be cured.
findings.explanation: The English adds a generalized routine of treating any enemy this way.

findings.highlight: that would give you even less right to interfere
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=あなた char=2]他人が口出しできる話じゃない
findings.governingReading: Rin says precisely because this concerns blood relatives, it is not a matter on which an outsider—read specifically as “you”—may comment.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the written outsider/ruby-you structure and invents a comparative “even less” right.

findings.highlight: on bad terms or in good harmony
findings.evidenceJa: いがみ合っているのか息が合っているのか
findings.governingReading: Kirei jokes that he cannot tell whether they are snarling at each other or perfectly in sync.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the comic contrast between hostility and simultaneous coordination.

findings.evidenceJa: 同じぐらい真剣に
findings.governingReading: Though seated apart, Shirou and Rin listen with equal seriousness.
findings.explanation: The English omits the symmetry between them.

findings.evidenceJa: あの爺以外
findings.governingReading: Rin contemptuously calls Zouken that old man.
findings.explanation: The English adds profanity absent from her wording.

findings.evidenceJa: あの吸血虫
findings.governingReading: Kirei calls Zouken that bloodsucking insect or parasite.
findings.explanation: The English changes the metaphor into a categorical supernatural identity.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂には悪いと思う
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels he is wronging Rin by insisting on hearing everything.
findings.explanation: The English sounds like pity for Rin rather than apology toward her.

findings.evidenceJa: 本来の神経と絡み合いながら全身に行き渡っている
findings.governingReading: The worm-derived nerves intertwine with Sakura’s original nerves and extend throughout her body.
findings.explanation: “Swarming” turns the distributed nerve network back into moving insects and obscures its integration.

findings.evidenceJa: 生命力たる魔力
findings.governingReading: The worms take magical energy specifically identified as Sakura’s life force.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the life-force equivalence that explains the mortal danger.

findings.evidenceJa: 身体を[ruby text=むし o2o=1]刻印に奪われる
findings.governingReading: After her mana is emptied, Sakura’s body will be taken over by the Crest, read as the worms.
findings.explanation: The English changes bodily possession into consumption and loses the written/ruby mechanism.

findings.highlight: Even the faintest trace of a foreign substance puts a human body through discomfort
findings.evidenceJa: 爪の先ほどの異物が混入しただけで不快感を訴え
findings.governingReading: A foreign body only the size of a fingernail tip makes the human body itself protest in discomfort.
findings.explanation: The English removes the concrete scale and the body-as-agent formulation.

findings.highlight: would easily be enough to kill you
findings.evidenceJa: 吐き気だけで死に至る程
findings.governingReading: The sensation would be so intolerable that nausea alone could bring death.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the startling claim that nausea itself could be fatal.

findings.evidenceJa: かけられた薬物
findings.governingReading: The substance applied to Sakura is described neutrally as a drug or chemical agent.
findings.explanation: The English categorically calls it poison.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=かつどう char=2]食事を開始する
findings.governingReading: When Sakura breaks the condition, the worms begin “feeding,” with the written word read as “activity.”
findings.explanation: The English keeps only activation and deletes that their punitive operation consists of feeding on her.

findings.highlight: Just listening to his words makes me go crazy
findings.evidenceJa: 聞き続けるだけでどうかしそうだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels he may lose control merely from continuing to listen.
findings.explanation: The English promotes an imminent destabilization into categorical insanity.

findings.evidenceJa: 身勝手な激情
findings.governingReading: Shirou suppresses a selfish, violent surge of passion.
findings.explanation: The English removes the intensity and violent force of his reaction.

findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜の精神が保つまい
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s psyche will probably be unable to endure if the condition continues.
findings.explanation: The English converts prognosis about endurance into categorical destruction.

findings.highlight: urge to cut off my arm
findings.evidenceJa: 腕ごとどうにかしたくなる
findings.governingReading: Rin periodically wants to do something drastic about the entire arm bearing her crest.
findings.explanation: The English specifies amputation, an act Rin does not state.

findings.evidenceJa: 人間の[ruby text=せいしん char=2]脳髄
findings.governingReading: The written text names the human brain or marrow of the brain, read as psyche.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the abstract ruby reading and deletes the physical brain.

findings.highlight: integrated itself into her Magic Circuits
findings.evidenceJa: 刻印虫は魔術回路となり、間桐桜の一部となっている
findings.governingReading: The crest worms themselves became circuit-like magical nerves and part of Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English instead says the worm integrated into Sakura’s preexisting Magic Circuits.

findings.highlight: wouldn’t be able to extract it
findings.evidenceJa: 解呪などできまい
findings.governingReading: Even the implanting practitioner likely could not dispel or undo the curse after this transformation.
findings.explanation: The English replaces magical curse-breaking with physical extraction.

findings.highlight: a miracle, or the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=きせき char=2]聖杯とやら
findings.governingReading: Kirei refers to the so-called Holy Grail, written “Holy Grail” and read “miracle.”
findings.explanation: The English incorrectly makes miracle and Holy Grail two alternatives.

findings.evidenceJa: 神父に向き直る
findings.governingReading: Rin turns back to face the priest after bowing.
findings.explanation: The English adds hostility by describing the movement as confrontation.

findings.highlight: hair and eye colors no longer reflect her heritage
findings.evidenceJa: 目も髪も遠坂の[ruby text=もの]色でなくなるほど
findings.governingReading: Sakura was altered until neither her eyes nor hair retained the Tohsaka family’s colors.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the specific erased family resemblance into abstract heritage.

findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯のお眼鏡にかなった
findings.governingReading: Rin asks whether Sakura suddenly met Zouken’s exacting standards or caught his approving eye.
findings.explanation: The English changes evaluation of her usefulness into interpersonal trust.

findings.highlight: using magical energy to maintain her Servant
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを行使する事で
findings.governingReading: Sakura began constantly consuming mana by exercising or deploying her Servant.
findings.explanation: The English narrows active Servant use to passive maintenance cost.

findings.evidenceJa: 戦わなければ体を乗っ取られて
findings.governingReading: If Sakura refuses battle, the worms will take over her body.
findings.explanation: A conditional English variant replaces possession with death.

findings.highlight: her body will also be destroyed
findings.evidenceJa: あの子の体は削られていく
findings.governingReading: Even if she fights, Sakura’s body is progressively worn away by mana consumption.
findings.explanation: The English turns gradual attrition into outright destruction.

findings.evidenceJa: 都合のいい駒
findings.governingReading: Sakura is a convenient pawn in Zouken’s strategy.
findings.explanation: The English loses the strategic game-piece image.

findings.evidenceJa: 歯がゆい
findings.governingReading: Kirei finds the prospect of events following Zouken’s design galling or intolerably frustrating.
findings.explanation: The English minimizes the reaction to slight irritation.

findings.evidenceJa: かけられた薬物を洗浄して
findings.governingReading: Kirei says he washed out the drug applied to Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English again hardens the neutral chemical description into poison.

findings.evidenceJa: 今の言峰は意外だった
findings.governingReading: What surprises Shirou is Kirei as he is behaving now, not merely the content of one utterance.
findings.explanation: The English narrows a character judgment to surprising words.

findings.highlight: this is too much even for that
findings.evidenceJa: 本当にとんでもないコトなのだと実感できる
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels how truly extraordinary or unthinkable Kirei’s sincere effort is.
findings.explanation: The English becomes vague and can sound like criticism of excessive priestly behavior.

findings.highlight: I can’t even stand up because I can’t think of anything
findings.evidenceJa: いまだ腰をあげられずにいる
findings.governingReading: Shirou remains seated, helpless and still unable to lift himself.
findings.explanation: The English invents inability to think as the physical cause.

findings.evidenceJa: 自らを撃つ事で暴走を止めた
findings.governingReading: Sakura struck or attacked herself with the earring agent to stop her rampage.
findings.explanation: “Shooting herself” falsely introduces a firearm or projectile action.

findings.evidenceJa: 自らの心を殺す事で
findings.governingReading: Sakura stopped the self Zouken could control by killing or shutting down her own heart/spirit.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the act to cognition and suggests destruction of her mind.

findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜の苦悶を聞きつけて
findings.governingReading: Kirei warns that Shirou may hear Sakura’s audible anguish or groans and burst in.
findings.explanation: The English specifies a scream not present in the source.

findings.evidenceJa: 押し入られては仕損じる
findings.governingReading: If Shirou bursts in, Kirei will botch or fail the procedure.
findings.explanation: The English adds categorical certainty to the predicted failure.

findings.highlight: you bear no responsibility for her sufferings
findings.evidenceJa: 苦悩を背負う義務もあるまい
findings.governingReading: Shirou has no obligation to shoulder the anguish of hearing Sakura’s treatment.
findings.explanation: The English changes an obligation to bear pain into causal or moral responsibility for Sakura’s suffering.

findings.evidenceJa: なんで、という声が出ない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot get the word “why” out as a voice.
findings.explanation: The English changes failure to voice a specific protest into generic sentence interruption.

findings.highlight: crimes I didn’t know I had committed
findings.evidenceJa: 俺でさえ知らない罪を指摘している
findings.governingReading: Kirei’s grave words point to a sin of which even Shirou is unaware.
findings.explanation: The English asserts that Shirou committed multiple crimes, converting accusation or implication into fact.

findings.highlight: She is a victim of sexual abuse
findings.evidenceJa: 実験台にされ続けてきた
findings.governingReading: Sakura was continually used as an experimental subject in the Matou succession process.
findings.explanation: A conditional English variant replaces prolonged experimentation with an explicit sexual-abuse claim.

findings.highlight: not a pure virgin, but a woman who knows men
findings.evidenceJa: 蟲に汚された[ruby text=あま char=2]魔女
findings.governingReading: Kirei calls Sakura a maiden contaminated by worms and a written “witch” read with a contemptuous woman term.
findings.explanation: A conditional English variant replaces the worm-and-witch formulation with factual claims about virginity and sexual experience.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=こいつ char=2]神父に言い負かされた
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he is not leaving because the priest—read contemptuously as “this guy”—defeated him in argument.
findings.explanation: The English deletes both the argumentative defeat and the written/ruby characterization of Kirei.

findings.highlight: I shouldn’t be allowed to care for Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を想ってはいけない筈だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou decides he must not think of Sakura while his head is incapable of coherent thought.
findings.explanation: The English turns temporary self-restraint in thinking into a moral prohibition on caring for her.

findings.highlight: she would have died under normal circumstances
findings.evidenceJa: 本来ならばあのまま死んでいた
findings.governingReading: Without Shirou’s intervention, the woman would have died as events stood.
findings.explanation: “Under normal circumstances” falsely presents death as the general norm rather than the counterfactual outcome of that attack.

findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方になる
findings.governingReading: Kirei recalls Shirou’s stated ideal of becoming an ally or champion of justice.
findings.explanation: “Superhero” trivializes and culturally reframes the work’s central ethical formula.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分を殺すかどうか
findings.governingReading: Kirei demands that Shirou decide whether, like Kiritsugu, he will kill or negate his own self for the sake of ideal and conviction.
findings.explanation: The English narrows total self-negation to relinquishing personal desires.

findings.evidenceJa: 科せられた十字のように重かった
findings.governingReading: The church door feels as heavy as a cross imposed upon Shirou as punishment or burden.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the cross being laid upon him.
